### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **6** documentable anchor(s).

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/api/error-catalog.mdx`  _(via invalid_number (literal, a string literal in validateOne))_

⛔ **1** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-5.mdx`  _(via invalid_number (literal, a string literal in validateOne))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **56** of **208** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **150** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 7858c1d16bb27ac9a5a6d3ae9db9d6dd7331d43d` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `a67a8afbfdfa41edbe70200ed0d624d11469a88f` — the merge of head `0dd08045be400cc0e17736de7cb884a180b0616e` into base `7858c1d16bb27ac9a5a6d3ae9db9d6dd7331d43d`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin a67a8afbfdfa41edbe70200ed0d624d11469a88f && git checkout a67a8afbfdfa41edbe70200ed0d624d11469a88f
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 7858c1d16bb27ac9a5a6d3ae9db9d6dd7331d43d 0dd08045be400cc0e17736de7cb884a180b0616e && git checkout -B drift-repro 7858c1d16bb27ac9a5a6d3ae9db9d6dd7331d43d && git merge --no-ff 0dd08045be400cc0e17736de7cb884a180b0616e

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 7858c1d16bb27ac9a5a6d3ae9db9d6dd7331d43d
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 7858c1d16bb27ac9a5a6d3ae9db9d6dd7331d43d` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `6d7035fec0ae4ba11b21e63485280e6b5964092f`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/system/validation-message.ts, packages/objectql/src/validation/record-validator.ts + packages/spec/src/data/field.zod.ts (`CurrencyConfigSchema`), packages/spec/src/data/field-value.zod.ts (the numeric class), packages/spec/src/api/errors.zod.ts (`FieldErrorCode`), docs/adr/0104-field-runtime-value-shape-contract.md, packages/spec/src/data/seed.zod.ts (`SeedRecordValueSchema`), packages/cli/src/commands/validate.ts, packages/cli/src/utils/bundle-seed-files.ts, packages/core/src/utils/import-coerce.ts, packages/runtime/src/dispatcher-error-vocabulary.ts, ui/packages/plugin-grid/src/ImportWizard.tsx, .changeset/27236-currency-object-value-lesson.md, PR #27233's file list at `c85e08be`

Inputs read: card #27236 (body; triage 6468450177; claim 6468731037; os-dev-report 6469929253), ruling 6464202770 on #27119 (Q2 = X), card #27182 and PR #27233 (overlap and ordering only), PR #27258 body, file list and the net diff against `main` at the head (merge-base `d745bb5e`), and the head's check-runs read to completion. Nothing was built, run or re-run.

### ① Derived judgments

Every accept-set and public-surface change the diff implies, each named right or wrong.

1. **Accept set: unchanged — right.** The only behavioural hunk is the numeric arm of `validateOne` (`isJudgedNumberType(t)`), where `fail('invalid_number')` becomes `fail('invalid_number', undefined, t === 'currency' && isPlainObjectValue(value) ? 'invalid_number_currency_object' : undefined)`. `fail`'s third parameter is `messageKey?: string`, and `buildFieldError` renders `args.messageKey ?? args.code`; the wire `code` is the first argument and stays `invalid_number`. Every value refused before is refused now, every value accepted before (a number, a string the numeric grammar reads) takes the unchanged second branch. The `FieldValidationError` keys (`field`, `code`, `message`, `label`) come from `buildFieldError`, which the diff does not touch.
2. **The lesson fires only for a `currency` field given a plain object — right.** `t` is `def.type`, so a `number`, `percent`, `rating`, `slider` or `progress` field keeps the plain sentence; a `formula` is outside `isJudgedNumberType` (`COMPUTED_VALUE_TYPES`). `isPlainObjectValue` refuses `null`, arrays and any non-`Object.prototype`/non-null prototype (`Date`, class instances), so a string, `[10]` and a `Date` keep the plain sentence. The #5922 operator-object gate runs before the per-type branches and refuses `{ $in: [...] }` as `invalid_type`/`invalid_value_shape`, so an operator object never reaches the lesson; `{ value, currency }` carries no operator key and falls through to the numeric arm. The seven objectql pins cover dynamic and fixed mode, insert and update, and the three controls (`'abc'`, `[10]`, an object on `number`).
3. **No client contract moves — right.** `FieldErrorCode` (`packages/spec/src/api/errors.zod.ts`, ADR-0114) is unchanged; `invalid_number_currency_object` is a catalog message key, the same code/messageKey split `invalid_value_shape`, `required_cleared`, `invalid_option_picklist_unresolved` and `value_domain_*` already use, and message keys never reach the wire. Every reader of `invalid_number` outside the two touched sources matches on `code`, not on text: `packages/runtime/src/dispatcher-error-vocabulary.ts` (three catalog rows, code only), `packages/core/src/utils/import-coerce.ts` (its own `import_invalid_number` sentence), `ui/packages/plugin-grid/src/ImportWizard.tsx` and its cellCheck tests (import codes), the rest import tests (`toMatchObject({ code: 'invalid_number' })`). The one text pin, `operator-object-write-value.test.ts:172` `'N must be a number'`, is a `number` field given an operator object: refused one gate earlier, and `number` is outside the lesson either way. REST ships `FieldValidationError.message` verbatim (validation-message.ts header); no REST or Console code parses it.
4. **Public surface: no export, type or schema change — right.** `BUILTIN_VALIDATION_MESSAGES` is typed as a Record of string to a Record of string to string (an open string-keyed map, no literal key union), so a new key changes no `.d.ts`; `isPlainObjectValue` is module-private; no `.describe()`, no authorable key. The spec generated-artifact gates have nothing to regenerate, and `Lint & Repo Gates` and `TypeScript Type Check` agree (below).
5. **One owning constant — right.** The sentence lives once per locale in the catalog; the validator passes only the key. The test's `startsWith('Amount is a currency amount: write it as a bare number')` is a pin on the rendered output, not a second copy the runtime reads.
6. **i18n — right, and no gate is owed.** validation-message.ts carries four catalogs (`en`, `zh-CN`, `ja-JP`, `es-ES`); the new key joins all four, with `{{label}}` in each and single-brace `{ value, currency }` that `interpolateValidationMessage`'s `{{name}}` regex cannot touch. These catalogs are platform constants outside the extract-and-gate bundle pipeline by design (the file header), and none of `scripts/check-i18n-*.mjs` reads the file; the gate that holds the four complete is the spec's own `every locale defines every message key` pin, which runs in `Test Core`.
7. **True under ruling X and ADR-0104 — right in substance; one cite placement to tidy (S1).** No locale spells a currency code or symbol (the spec pin checks a 3-capital pattern and `$¥€£` after stripping `ADR-0104`), so the lesson names no default. "A bare number" is ADR-0104 D1. "The fixed mode's defaultCurrency" and "under the dynamic mode (the default) the tenant default currency" match `CurrencyConfigSchema` at the head (`currencyMode` default `'dynamic'`; dynamic displays in the tenant default) and ruling 6464202770 Q2 = X. `defaultCurrency` still defaults to `'CNY'` at the head (ruling G3 removes it on another card); the lesson does not depend on that default, so it stays true after G3 lands.
8. **Overlap and ordering with PR #27233 — right.** The two file lists (5 against 26 at #27233 head `c85e08be`, still its head at review time) intersect in zero paths; this PR does not touch `field.zod.ts`, `field-value.zod.ts` or ADR-0104, all #27233 files. Leaving the `valueSchemaFor('currency')` arm alone is both what the serial constraint requires and what the measurement supports: `currency` is a member of the numeric class (`field-value.zod.ts:65`), and the record validator judges that class in its own arm without consulting `valueSchemaFor`, so a sentence there would never reach a record writer. "Lands after #27233" stands as the card wrote it.
9. **Out-of-scope finding (`os validate` passes a non-number currency seed value) — real as described.** `SeedRecordValueSchema` is `z.unknown()` with a `superRefine` that judges only seed file references; `validate.ts` reaches seed rows only through `collectSeedFiles` (`bundle-seed-files.ts`, file references again); the lint seed rules are `validateSeedReplaySafety` and `validateSeedStateMachine`. No door judges a seed value against its field type before the record validator at seed load. The dev reported it and did not expand scope, as Prime Directive #10 asks; it is a card for the seat to file, not a change here.

### ② Semver level

- Changeset `.changeset/27236-currency-object-value-lesson.md`: `'@objectstack/spec': patch`, `'@objectstack/objectql': patch`. Both are published (`private` unset, 18.2.0), and they are the only two packages whose `src` the diff moves. Level right: `Clause-②: no` with no arm and `Metadata-protocol: none` take `patch`.
- `Clause-②: no` is true: the accept set is the same before and after (①.1). `Metadata-protocol: none` is true: nothing an author can write changes (①.4). Both declarations are line-initial in the PR body and the changeset.
- The ADR-0087 marker `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` is present and its facts hold (no authorable key, export or stored shape moves). Not a breaking changeset, so no migration is owed; the body still states what to do (nothing).
- Title carries no `!`; nothing here is a release act.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Dev flag: `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` NOT MEASURED locally.** CI measures it in `ci.yml` job `build-core`, context **`Build Core`**, step "Every published require entry point actually loads" (it needs a real `dist/`, which is why it lives there and not in the lint job). Conclusion on this head: job 122837326812 `success`, and its step 14 "Every published require entry point actually loads" ran to `success` (not skipped), so the gate was measured, not only hosted.
- **Required contexts on this head** (`REQUIRED_CONTEXTS` in `scripts/check-required-contexts.mjs` on `origin/main` has **ten** rows, not nine: `Test UI` and `Live E2E UI` both joined it), every one read to completion:

  | context | conclusion |
  |:--|:--|
  | `Lint & Repo Gates` | `success` |
  | `TypeScript Type Check` | `success` |
  | `Test Core` | `success` (all eight shards `success`) |
  | `Build Core` | `success` |
  | `Governed Surface Queue Guard` | `success` |
  | `Lint UI` | `skipped` — the job's `if:` reads the `filter` job's `ui` output, which is false on a diff with no `ui/` path; a paths-filter skip by design, not a missing run |
  | `Build & E2E UI` | `success` |
  | `Type Check UI` | `success` |
  | `Test UI` | `success` |
  | `Live E2E UI` | `success` |

- All 49 check-runs on the head completed; every conclusion is `success` or `skipped`, none failed.
- **Dev flag: ablation.** Read, not re-run: 2 failed / 131 passed with the `t === 'currency' && isPlainObjectValue(value)` condition ablated, restored blob equals HEAD. Consistent with the diff (only the two lesson pins depend on that condition).
- **`open_questions`: none** in the os-dev-report. Nothing to answer or escalate.
- **Claim identity.** Claim 6468731037 names branch `claude/project-thread-u4sy2p`, the PR's head ref; no later `Claim:` on the card. The dev's report comment is its record; it wrote no second claim.
- **Should-fix S1 (non-blocking, wording):** in all four locales the parenthetical `(ADR-0104)` closes the clause "under the dynamic mode (the default) the tenant default currency". ADR-0104 decides the bare-number shape (D1) and says nothing about a tenant default; that half is ruling 6464202770 Q2 = X and the `currencyMode` describe in `field.zod.ts`. Move the cite next to the shape clause ("write it as a bare number (ADR-0104), ...") or leave the tenant-default clause uncited. The spec pin only asserts `ADR-0104` is present, so it holds either way.
- **Observation (not the dev's):** the brief's premise of nine required contexts is one short of the register; recorded above so the next review reads ten.
